description: Produce the hardware acceptance runbook and close the verification gaps that cannot be closed in the sandbox. Nothing in FEAT-002 through FEAT-004 is actually proven until it runs on the Pi: the sandbox has no docker compose plugin, no udevadm, no shellcheck, and no scanner. This feature writes deploy/ACCEPTANCE.md as an ordered checklist the human executes on the Raspberry Pi, with the exact command and the exact expected output for each check, plus a contingency plan for the one design assumption that carries real risk. The agent must NOT mark any hardware check as passed — the agent's deliverable is the runbook and a correctly-recorded set of deferred items.
steps: Create deploy/ACCEPTANCE.md. Open it with a statement of the single acceptance question this whole task exists to answer: does the Pi boot with no scanner attached and serve a usable web UI, and does it start reading the scanner whenever the scanner appears. Every check below either proves that or guards a regression against it.

Check T0 — close the deferred compose validation. On the Pi: `cd /opt/pantry && sudo docker compose config`. Expected: the merged configuration prints with no error, showing the /dev/input bind mount and the device_cgroup_rules entry, and showing no `devices:` key. This is the schema validation that could not be run in the sandbox because the compose plugin is absent there.

Check T1 — the headline acceptance test. With the scanner physically UNPLUGGED, reboot the Pi. After boot: `sudo docker compose ps` shows the pantry container running; `curl http://localhost:$HOST_PORT/health` returns status ok with scanner.connected false; the web UI loads from another device on the network. This is the exact scenario that fails today. Record the full health payload verbatim.

Check T2 — hot-plug pickup. With the container already running from T1, plug the scanner in. Within 30 seconds (the backoff cap), `curl http://localhost:$HOST_PORT/health` must report scanner.connected true and scanner.grabbed true. Then scan a product barcode and confirm an entry appears in the scan queue in the UI. Record how long pickup actually took. If connected becomes true but grabbed stays false, note it — the app tolerates a failed EVIOCGRAB and keeps working, but the scanner's keystrokes will also reach the console.

Check T3 — hot-unplug does not take the UI down. While the container is running with the scanner connected, capture `sudo docker inspect -f '{{.State.StartedAt}}' pantry`, then unplug the scanner. Confirm: the web UI still loads; /health still returns status ok with scanner.connected false; and StartedAt is UNCHANGED, proving the container was not restarted or recreated. This is the specific regression that the rejected systemd-unit design would have introduced, so it is worth an explicit guard.

Check T4 — replug reconnects. Plug the scanner back in, confirm scanner.connected returns to true within 30 seconds, and scan a barcode to confirm end-to-end recovery. Confirm StartedAt is still unchanged across the whole unplug/replug cycle.

Check T5 — boot with the scanner attached. Reboot with the scanner plugged in. Confirm the container comes up and the scanner is connected without any manual intervention. Note that at boot the container may start before udev has created the symlink; the backoff loop is expected to absorb that, so confirm it resolves on its own rather than needing a restart.

Check T6 — clean install from scratch. On a clean state (`sudo docker compose down`, then move /opt/pantry aside), run `sudo ./setup.sh install` from a fresh copy of deploy/ and confirm it completes end to end and finishes with a passing `sudo ./setup.sh status`. This is the path that is broken today because the current script never copies the systemd/ and udev/ subdirectories it later reads from.

Check T7 — idempotency and the rollback-safety regression. Set PANTRY_IMAGE_TAG in /opt/pantry/.env to a specific commit SHA, run `sudo ./setup.sh install` a second time, then `grep PANTRY_IMAGE_TAG /opt/pantry/.env`. The pinned SHA must survive, and `sudo docker compose ps` must show the pinned image still running rather than latest. The current script fails this check by overwriting .env and then redeploying latest.

Check T8 — the security property. Confirm that granting the container the input class did not grant it every keyboard. On the host run `ls -l /dev/input/event*` and record the owner, group and mode of every node: the scanner's node must be group 65532 mode 0640, and every other node must remain root:input mode 0600 and therefore unreadable by uid 65532. Then confirm the health payload reports exactly one device path, the scanner's. Note explicitly that the container is distroless so this cannot be checked by shelling in — the host-side permissions plus the health payload are the evidence.

Check T9 — the lint and syntax checks that the sandbox could not run. On the Pi or any machine with the tools: `udevadm verify /etc/udev/rules.d/99-pantry-scanner.rules` (available on systemd 251 and newer; if the subcommand is unavailable, use `udevadm test $(udevadm info -q path -n /dev/input/pantry-scanner)` and confirm the rule matches and the SYMLINK, GROUP and MODE are applied) and `shellcheck deploy/setup.sh`. Record both results.

Check T10 — update timer controls. Run `sudo ./setup.sh freeze` and confirm `systemctl is-enabled pantry-update.timer` reports masked; run `sudo ./setup.sh thaw` and confirm it is restored. Confirm that `install` without --with-updates left the timer not enabled.

Write a contingency section for the one assumption with real risk: device_cgroup_rules must actually be honored on the Pi's cgroup layout. Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm uses cgroup v2, where Docker implements device rules as eBPF filters. Document how to tell the failure modes apart from the lastError string in /health, because the three look similar and have different fixes: ENOENT / 'no such file or directory' means the udev rule did not match and no symlink was created, so fix the rule; EACCES / 'permission denied' means the node's group does not match GID 65532, so fix GROUP in the rule or SCANNER_GID in .env; EPERM / 'operation not permitted' means the device cgroup denied the open, which is the case that would indicate device_cgroup_rules is not taking effect.

In that same contingency section, state the fallback if and only if EPERM is observed: re-test with the rule widened to 'c 13:* rwm' to determine whether the mode string is the problem, and record the finding. Do NOT fall back to `privileged: true`, and do NOT reintroduce a `devices:` entry, since that would restore the original boot failure. If the cgroup approach genuinely cannot work, stop and escalate with the evidence rather than working around it.
Add a results table to deploy/ACCEPTANCE.md with a row per check (T0-T10) and columns for result, date, and notes, left blank for the human to fill in. Do not pre-fill any result.

In the feature's findings, list every verification this task deferred to hardware and state plainly that the agent did not execute them. Specifically: compose schema validation, udev rule matching, shellcheck, and all scanner behavior. Do not describe the task as verified.
Commit with a message like `docs: add hardware acceptance runbook for scanner hot-plug`.
acceptance_criteria: deploy/ACCEPTANCE.md exists and opens with the single acceptance question the task exists to answer.
Checks T0 through T10 are each documented with an exact command and an exact expected result.
T1 covers boot with the scanner unplugged and is identified as the headline acceptance test.
T3 includes the docker inspect StartedAt before/after comparison proving the container is not restarted when the scanner is unplugged.
T8 covers the host-side permission evidence for the security property and notes the distroless constraint.
A contingency section distinguishes ENOENT, EACCES, and EPERM from the health lastError string, with the correct fix for each.
The contingency section explicitly forbids falling back to privileged: true or to a devices: entry.
A results table with rows T0-T10 exists with all result cells left blank.
findings lists every deferred verification and states the agent did not execute them.
verification: deploy/ACCEPTANCE.md exists and contains headings or rows for T0 through T11 inclusive of the contingency section.
`grep -c 'T[0-9]' deploy/ACCEPTANCE.md` confirms all eleven checks are present.
`grep -n 'privileged' deploy/ACCEPTANCE.md` shows it only in the prohibition, never as a recommended fallback.
`grep -n 'StartedAt' deploy/ACCEPTANCE.md` shows the T3 container-restart guard.
`grep -n 'ENOENT\|EACCES\|EPERM' deploy/ACCEPTANCE.md` shows all three failure modes documented.
Confirm by reading that no result cell in the results table is pre-filled.
This feature adds documentation only: `git diff master --stat` for this commit must show deploy/ACCEPTANCE.md and nothing else.
